questions.q:
But-2-yne and hydrogen (one mole each) are separately treated with (i) Pd/C and (ii) Na/liq. NH3 to give the products X and Y respectively.
Identify the incorrect statements.
A. X and Y are stereoisomers.
B. Dipole moment of X is zero.
C. Boiling point of X is higher than Y.
D. X and Y react with O3/Zn + H2O to give different products.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explain: Here the question wants the INCORRECT statements, so read carefully. Partial hydrogenation of but-2-yne over Pd/C gives cis-but-2-ene (X) by syn addition, and Na/liq. NH3 gives trans-but-2-ene (Y) by anti addition. So X and Y are cis-trans (geometrical) isomers, which are stereoisomers, and A is correct. The cis isomer has its two C-CH3 bond dipoles on the same side, so it has a net dipole moment and B (X has zero dipole) is incorrect. The polar cis isomer has stronger dipole-dipole attraction and a higher boiling point, so C is correct. Ozonolysis of either isomer gives the same product, 2 CH3CHO, so D is incorrect. Incorrect: B and D.

questions.q: Identify (P): the vicinal dibromide shown is treated with (i) Zn, heat and then (ii) HBr to give (P), the major product.
questions.explain: Zn with heat removes two vicinal Br atoms and makes a C=C, giving a cyclopentene. One carbon of that C=C sits next to the ring carbon carrying CH3, and the other next to the ring carbon carrying the ethyl group. HBr adds H+ to one alkene carbon and gives a secondary carbocation. A 1,2-hydride shift from the neighbouring ring carbon that bears CH3 moves the charge onto it, giving a tertiary carbocation. Tertiary is more stable than secondary, so this shift happens. Br- then attacks that carbon. The major product has Br and CH3 on the same ring carbon: a tertiary bromide, with the ethyl group left on the ring. That is option D. The trap options A, B and C keep Br on a secondary carbon.

questions.q: Consider the following reaction: the dibromoalkane shown (a four-carbon chain with both Br atoms on the same carbon) + 2 NaNH2 gives X. Then X with (i) NaNH2 and (ii) isopropyl bromide gives Y. The product Y formed is:
questions.explain: Two equivalents of NaNH2 remove 2 HBr from the dibromide (double dehydrohalogenation) and give a four-carbon alkyne, X. The next NaNH2 pulls off the acidic H of a terminal alkyne to make the acetylide ion, so X must be but-1-yne, CH3CH2-C≡CH. The acetylide then attacks isopropyl bromide by SN2 and joins the isopropyl group to the triple-bond carbon. The product is CH3CH2-C≡C-CH(CH3)2. Numbering from the isopropyl end gives the methyl on C2 and the triple bond at C3, so Y is 2-methylhex-3-yne. The 2-yne options are traps: they would need the triple bond at the wrong spot. 'Isopropylbut-1-yne' is not a valid IUPAC name.

questions.q:
The incorrect statements regarding geometrical isomerism are:
A. Propene shows geometrical isomerism.
B. Trans isomer has identical atoms/groups on the opposite sides of the double bond.
C. Cis-but-2-ene has higher dipole moment than trans-but-2-ene.
D. 2-Methylbut-2-ene shows two geometrical isomers.
E. Trans-isomer has lower melting point than cis isomer.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explain: The question asks for the INCORRECT statements, so test each one. Geometrical isomerism needs two different groups on each carbon of the C=C. A (propene): the CH2 end has two H, so there is no isomerism. A is incorrect. B is the definition of the trans isomer, so it is correct. C: cis-but-2-ene has a net dipole moment and trans cancels to about zero, so C is correct. D (2-methylbut-2-ene): one carbon carries two CH3 groups, so there is no geometrical isomerism at all. D is incorrect. E: trans isomers pack better in the crystal and usually have the higher melting point, so E is incorrect. Incorrect statements: A, D and E.
